- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) and price is trending down, model often overcorrects downward; avoid sharp drops; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias.
- After a price spike (≥ 1.5% above recent mean), model frequently overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% in next 2–3 periods.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply upward bias of 0.5–1.0% to next forecast.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending sideways, model often underestimates volatility; increase forecast variance by 0.3–0.7%.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early-term price stability; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% in first 5–7 days if sentiment is weak.
